description:
The "Raising the Standard of Tiatr" scheme is an initiative by the Government of Goa aimed at promoting and preserving the traditional art form of Tiatr. 

Tiatr is a form of musical theatre that originated in Goa and has significant cultural importance among the Goan community. 

The scheme was launched on August 1, 2021. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to Tiatr artists and groups to enhance the quality of their performances. 

The government aims to uplift the standards of Tiatr by providing support for production costs, training, and other related expenses. 

The scheme has set a measurable target of supporting at least 50 Tiatr productions annually. 

Each production is eligible for financial assistance of up to INR 2 lakh. 

This financial support is intended to cover expenses such as stage setup, costumes, and promotional activities. 

The scheme also aims to provide training programs for aspiring Tiatr artists. 

These training programs are designed to enhance the skills of performers, directors, and writers involved in Tiatr. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 1 crore for the initial phase of this scheme. 

This budget is expected to be reviewed and potentially increased based on the scheme's performance and uptake. 

Eligibility for financial assistance under this scheme is primarily focused on Tiatr artists and groups based in Goa. 

Individual artists must be at least 18 years old to qualify for assistance. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for the scheme. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a commitment to Tiatr and a history of participation in the art form. 

Tiatr groups must be registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 to be eligible for funding. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

Interested artists or groups must submit an application form to the Directorate of Art and Culture, Goa. 

The application form can be obtained from the Directorate's official website or office. 

Along with the application form, applicants must provide a detailed project proposal outlining their production plans. 

This proposal should include a budget breakdown and a timeline for the production. 

Additionally, applicants must submit proof of registration for groups or a portfolio for individual artists. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture reviews all applications. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days from the date of submission. 

Once approved, funds are disbursed in two installments. 

The first installment of 50% is released upon approval. 

The second installment is released upon submission of a completion report and financial statements. 

The scheme is designed to be implemented by the Directorate of Art and Culture, Goa. 

This department is responsible for overseeing the promotion of various cultural activities in the state. 

For any inquiries regarding the scheme, individuals can contact the Directorate at their office located in Panaji, Goa. 

The contact number for the Directorate is +91-832-222-1541. 

The scheme also aims to promote Tiatr beyond Goa. 

By enhancing the quality of productions, the government hopes to attract larger audiences. 

This includes organizing festivals and events that showcase Tiatr performances. 

The government plans to collaborate with educational institutions to introduce Tiatr as part of cultural studies. 

This initiative aims to instill appreciation for Tiatr among younger generations. 

The scheme is part of a broader effort to preserve and promote Goan culture and heritage. 

Tiatr has faced challenges in recent years due to changing entertainment preferences. 

The government recognizes the need to adapt and modernize Tiatr while preserving its traditional roots. 

Through this scheme, the government hopes to create a sustainable ecosystem for Tiatr. 

This includes ensuring that artists receive fair compensation for their work. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of community involvement in Tiatr productions. 

Local communities are encouraged to participate in performances and support their local artists. 

The government has also proposed the establishment of a Tiatr Academy. 

This academy would serve as a hub for training and development of Tiatr artists. 

It would provide workshops, seminars, and mentorship programs. 

The goal is to create a new generation of skilled Tiatr performers and writers. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of promoting cultural tourism in Goa. 

By enhancing the quality of Tiatr, the government aims to attract tourists interested in cultural experiences. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the local economy by generating employment opportunities. 

It is estimated that each Tiatr production can create jobs for at least 20 individuals. 

This includes roles such as actors, musicians, stagehands, and costume designers. 

The government also plans to document and archive Tiatr performances. 

This initiative aims to preserve the history and evolution of Tiatr for future generations. 

The scheme is expected to run for an initial period of three years. 

At the end of this period, the government will assess its impact and effectiveness. 

Feedback from artists and audiences will be collected to improve the scheme. 

The government is committed to making necessary adjustments based on this feedback. 

Overall, the "Raising the Standard of Tiatr" scheme represents a significant step towards preserving and promoting this unique Goan art form. 

It reflects the government's recognition of the cultural value of Tiatr and its importance to the identity of the Goan people. 

Through targeted financial assistance and training, the scheme aims to ensure that Tiatr continues to thrive in the years to come. 

This initiative is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting the arts and cultural heritage of Goa. 

The scheme is a vital part of the broader cultural policy framework of the Government of Goa. 

It underscores the importance of investing in the arts as a means of fostering community engagement and cultural pride. 

The government hopes that through this scheme, Tiatr will not only survive but flourish in the modern era.
